patterns.matches: Any subdomain of atlassian.net — and the apex domain itself — at any path depth
That exact host, any path below it
A bare host: matches all of its subpaths
* stays inside one path segment; ** or a trailing * crosses segments
Everything — but you don't need it; unmatched links already go to your fallback

actions.body: Open in a browser or app, named by its bundle ID. A Chrome web app (installed with Install page as app) works too: pick it under Web apps in the rule editor, or osascript -e 'id of app "ClickUp"' prints its bundle ID. The link opens in the web app's own window, in the profile the web app is installed in, or in the rule's profile if this Mac has it. Finding the installed profile needs Full Disk Access; without it, set the profile's directory (Profile 1) on the rule in the config file, or the link goes to your fallback browser. A link from a different site than the web app's goes to your fallback browser, because the web app would drop it.

Open in a specific browser profile, by the name listed in Settings → Browsers (for Firefox, what firefox -P takes). Chromium browsers also accept the profile directory (Default, Profile 1), but a directory can mean a different profile on another Mac, so the rule editor saves the name. Listing profiles needs Full Disk Access; without it, a Chromium profile still works if you type its directory into the config file, but a rule that uses a profile name, like any Firefox profile rule, falls back to your fallback browser.
Rewrite the link to a native app deep link. Works whether or not the rewriter is enabled in Settings → Deep Links.

Show the picker and let you choose at click time. Links sent to the picker while it is open collect in one list; choose a browser to open them all, or copy them on separate lines. Esc or clicking away cancels the whole list. In Settings → Browsers → Picker appearance you can lay the picker out as a horizontal row (←/→ to move, ↑/↓ to jump a row), show icons only, and change the icon size. The picker can also be your fallback for every unmatched link: "fallback": { "app": "picker" }.
Copy the link instead of opening it.

sync.label: First Mac
sync.body: the dialog says iCloud Drive has no Junction rules yet. Choose Upload This Mac's Rules.

sync.label: Each other Mac
sync.body: wait until the copy has downloaded to the Junction folder in iCloud Drive, then choose Use iCloud's Rules. If the dialog says there are no rules yet, cancel and try again later, or this Mac's rules replace the ones you synced. If the rules already match, sync starts without asking.

sync.label: Routing
sync.body: each Mac still routes from its own config.json, so links work offline and junction test reads the same file as always.

sync.label: Conflicts
sync.body: the newest change wins. The rules it replaced, like the set you didn't keep when turning sync on, are saved as config.backup.json next to your config file. An invalid edit stays on this Mac and isn't uploaded.

sync.label: Browser profiles
sync.body: starting sync with this Mac's rules swaps Chromium profile directories (Profile 1) in your rules for profile names, because a directory can be a different profile on another Mac. Reading the names needs Full Disk Access; without it, directories stay as they are.

sync.label: Turning it off
sync.body: stops this Mac from syncing and leaves the iCloud copy in place for your other Macs.

menubarActions.label: Recent links
menubarActions.body: the last 10 links Junction routed, in a submenu. In memory only — never written to disk.

menubarActions.label: Rules
menubarActions.body: every rule in match order, checked when it's on. Click one to turn it off or on without opening Settings; Edit Rules… opens the Rules pane.

menubarActions.label: Settings
menubarActions.body: fallback (a browser, or the ask-every-time picker), rules, browsers and profiles — including which appear in the picker and how it looks (a vertical list or a horizontal row, with or without names, any icon size) — deep links, iCloud sync, updates.

menubarActions.label: Updates
menubarActions.body: a check runs on its own; the icon gets a dot and the menu offers Update to … when one is ready.

troubleshooting.title: macOS refuses to open the app
troubleshooting.body: Junction isn't notarized yet, so macOS quarantines it. Clear the flag with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Junction.app, or right-click Junction.app → Open → Open.

troubleshooting.title: Nothing routes at all
troubleshooting.body: Junction only sees links when it is the default browser — that's the one step it can't work without. Re-select it under System Settings → Desktop & Dock → Default web browser.

troubleshooting.title: Links open in the wrong place
troubleshooting.body: Almost always precedence: a broader rule above is catching the link first. Run junction test <url> — it prints the matching rule and the decision without opening anything.

troubleshooting.title: No browser profiles to choose from
troubleshooting.body: macOS may block Junction from reading your browsers' profile lists, and it never asks first. Turn on Junction under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access, then click Check Again or Refresh in Settings → Browsers. If Junction is already on there, select it, remove it with −, and add it again — the switch can stay on after macOS stops honoring it. Junction only reads each browser's list of profile names.

troubleshooting.title: A rule opens the fallback instead of its app
troubleshooting.body: Junction degrades to the fallback rather than opening the wrong thing — a browser profile that isn't on this Mac, an app that isn't installed, an unknown rewriter, or a link from outside a web app's site all land there. The menu-bar icon flags an invalid config, and the last-good rules stay live until you fix it.

troubleshooting.title: iCloud sync shows a problem
troubleshooting.body: Sync never touches routing: each Mac keeps using its own rules until the problem is fixed, and Settings → General says what's wrong. If iCloud Drive is off, turn it on in System Settings → Apple Account → iCloud. If Junction can't read it, allow access under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Files and Folders. If the file in iCloud Drive was deleted, turn sync off and on to upload this Mac's rules again.

troubleshooting.title: Slack deep links open the browser
troubleshooting.body: Slack permalinks don't carry the team ID the app needs. Add the workspace in Settings → Deep Links — type it or paste a Slack link, and Junction reads the ID from the signed-in Slack app; unmapped workspaces open in the browser rather than on the wrong screen.

unsupported: Firefox containers are an extension feature with no launch-flag equivalent — Firefox profiles are supported.
roadmap: MVP under active development. Planned for v1.1+: redirect and shortener unwrapping (opt-in), mailto: routing, time- and network-based conditions, and Shortcuts actions.
